messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — we just got an SLO-burn alert on hosted-infer-starter (p95 latency > 1200ms + 5xx spike). Support also opened an escalated ticket complaining about client errors and billing anomalies. Posting initial findings.

Maya Patel: Alerts: SRE SLO alert  #slo-burn hosted-infer-starter > https://redwood.internal/alerts/INC-6124 : triggered at 2026-03-15T09:22Z. Pager fired.

Maya Patel: Early signal: high rate of 502/504 from edge-proxy -> ingress-gateway. Error logs show repeated `auth: token fetch failed` followed by short-circuited 502s. Support-bot forwarded a billing spike graph where customer X saw doubled request charge during the incident window.

Liam O'Connor: I'm looking at traces — many requests show successful client -> edge handoff but a gap between edge and backend (no downstream span). That smells like token exchange/backpressure at edge. Trace example: trace_id=abc123 (partial). There are gaps 100–300ms then drop.

Sajal Rao: Pasted relevant log snippet from edge-proxy (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T09:21:45Z edge-proxy auth: fetching token for svc-account inference-proxy
2026-03-15T09:21:45Z edge-proxy auth: token fetch failed: 503 service unavailable (upstream auth-server)
2026-03-15T09:21:45Z edge-proxy request: client_id=acct-xyz path=/v1/generate status=502 latency_ms=5
2026-03-15T09:21:46Z edge-proxy auth: retry token fetch (attempt=2) latency_ms=350
2026-03-15T09:21:46Z edge-proxy request: client_id=acct-xyz path=/v1/generate status=504 latency_ms=1205
```

Sajal Rao: The pattern: auth call fails -> edge blocks or retries -> downstream request either 502 quick-fail or 504 after waiting. That could cause duplicate client retry behavior (support reported increased tokenized charges).

Emily Chen: Query I used in logs UI to pull the correlated errors (KQL):
```
index=prod_edge_logs service=edge-proxy | where path like "/v1/%" and (status==502 or status==504) | parse "auth: token fetch failed*" as auth_err | stats count() by auth_err, status, bin(1m)
```

Emily Chen: Prometheus alert rule for the SLO burn: `sum(rate(edge_5xx_total[5m])) / sum(rate(edge_requests_total[5m])) > 0.02` — it crossed 4% briefly.

Raman Singh: Are auth-server healthchecks OK? I see a churn on auth instances last night (deploy) — maybe a bad rollout left a small percent of instances unhealthy and LB routed traffic to them.

Maya Patel: Good call. Ops-bot health summary (from deploy bot): auth-service deploy at 2026-03-15T03:10Z, 4/6 pods ready for ~5m, then flapped 2 pods from 03:15–03:18Z. Correlation window lines up.

Liam O'Connor: Repro steps I ran from staging to mimic behavior (note: auth TTL=60s in staging):
1) Start a curl hammer (concurrency=8) against /v1/generate with a small prompt.
2) Simultaneously kill 2 auth replicas (kubectl scale deployment auth-service --replicas=1)
3) Observe edge logs and client retries -> expect 502 / 504 mix and some duplicate upstream attempts.

Liam O'Connor: Curl example used for repro:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -w "%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://hosted.api.redwood/v1/generate &
done
```

Sajal Rao: I also found a log pattern showing token refresh fallback created a synchronous call on request path (we should be async). Code path: `getOrRefreshToken()` is called inline when token missing; if auth is slow, request blocks.

Emily Chen: Suggestion: change `getOrRefreshToken()` to return cached token and kick off background refresh when TTL < 5s instead of blocking. That avoids head-of-line blocking under auth slowness.

Raman Singh: Short-term mitigation: implement circuit-breaker around auth fetch in edge-proxy — after N consecutive failures mark token-service degraded and return 429 with `Retry-After` or use cached token (even if slightly stale) for up to 30s. That will reduce 5xx spike.

Maya Patel: Action items:
- @Liam O'Connor: run the staging repro and post full log traces and flamegraphs (owner) — ETA 2h.
- @Sajal Rao: open a PR to make token refresh async + add defensive caching (owner) — ETA EOD.
- @Raman Singh: add a temporary circuit-breaker + 429 fallback in edge-proxy config and roll to canary (owner) — ETA 4h.
- @Emily Chen: add a log correlation dashboard widget: auth.failures by pod + edge. (owner) — ETA tomorrow.

support-bot: Support ticket #SUP-9125 updated — told customer X we are investigating auth token instability causing request duplication and billing noise. Support asked for customer-facing mitigation (we can offer credits if confirmed).

Maya Patel: Quick note on billing: duplicate request retries can double counted tokens/units on our metering if they retry across different model shards. We'll need to run a billing reconciliation job for affected window 2026-03-15T09:20–09:40Z. @finance-sre FYI.

Liam O'Connor: Related observability queries I ran (PromQL):
```
sum(rate(edge_5xx_total{service="edge-proxy"}[1m])) by (status)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="edge-proxy"}[5m])) by (le))
```

Sajal Rao: One more gotcha found: token cache keyed only by service account id, not by region. If auth LB is regional and we fallback across region, cache misses spike. PR to add region tag to cache key in review.

Emily Chen: I'll attach a screenshot of the dashboard and the KQL and Prom queries to the support ticket.

Maya Patel: Follow-up plan: We'll monitor the canary after Raman's config. If we see reduced 5xx and stable auth success rate we'll promote. Also plan a postmortem draft tomorrow. If billing reconciliation confirms customer impact, coordinate credits and finalize support comms.

Raman Singh: Rolling canary with circuit-breaker now (canary = 5%): container image edge-proxy:v2026-03-15-canary-02. Watch channel `#deployments` for rollout status.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started: rollout_id=rl-8892 -> 5% traffic. Health checks streaming.

Liam O'Connor: Canary looks good so far — 5xx rate down to baseline within 10m. Will keep monitoring for 30m then approve.

Maya Patel: Great. I'll draft the incident stub and assign the postmortem. Thanks all. :heart:

Emily Chen: Adding labels: incident_type=auth-induced-5xx, impact=customer-billing, severity=P2.

Maya Patel: Closing notes: root cause likely transient auth-service rollout/health + sync token refresh on request path + cache key miss by region. Fixes: async refresh + region-aware cache + circuit-breaker. We'll track PRs and verification in this thread.

support-bot: Customer communication prepared — waiting on billing reconciliation results before sending credit offer.

Maya Patel: End of thread summary saved to /ops/incidents/2026-03-15-auth-5xx-draft.md and assigned to @Maya Patel for PM writeup.
